lines.text: Most of us blame the last thing we ate.
But your gut runs on a delay.
Food takes about twenty-nine hours, on average, to travel all the way through.
And eating something new can push along what you ate before.
So the meal on your plate gets caught in the act,
while the real reason may be lunch. Or yesterday.
Cut the wrong food, and often nothing changes. Except your plate gets smaller.
One day can't show you a delay.
Get Regular lines up your meals, symptoms and bathroom trips, day by day, so your pattern can show itself.
Your gut's been keeping time. Start keeping notes.
